title: E0049: Invalid builtin argument
plain_english: This rule reports builtin calls whose literal arguments are invalid and would make PHP throw a `ValueError` at runtime.
why_matters: These argument errors fail at runtime, often on a specific code path. Catching them statically avoids avoidable crashes and makes the intended input constraints explicit.
bad_example:
<?php
function bad(array $items): array
{
    return array_chunk($items, 0); // invalid size
}
what_it_checks: `str_split()` and `mb_str_split()` with a non-positive chunk length
`array_combine()` with literal arrays of different lengths
`random_int()`, `mt_rand()`, and `rand()` with a minimum greater than the maximum
